aiClips.aiLine: Several companies are investigating what appears to be a new hacking campaign. Experts are saying this is an advanced AI-driven worm that behaves unlike anything they've seen before.

candidates.name: 01-cbsmornings-china-ai-spy
candidates.event: Anthropic report that a Chinese state-backed group used Claude Code to automate most of an espionage campaign against about 30 organisations
candidates.speaker: anchor at desk (Tony Dokoupil) to 8.5 s, then anchor voice over an Anthropic quote card
candidates.quote: [This morning,] China is accused of using AI to spy on tech companies, financial institutions, and government agencies. It's all from the AI firm Anthropic, which says its own AI software was used in the first documented case of a worldwide cyber attack with minimal human involvement. The AI is doing the work.
candidates.onScreenText: CBS MORNINGS | A.I. USED IN CHINESE CYBERATTACK (lower third, legible at 480p). From ~8.5 s a full-screen card: ANTHROPIC '...the first documented case of a large-scale cyberattack executed without substantial human intervention.' The first ~1.1 s still carry the previous story's lower third (COLLEGE ATHLETIC DIR. SHOT ON CAMPUS IN CALIFORNIA).
candidates.picture: Anchor in dark suit at the CBS Mornings desk, warm orange studio; then blue circuit-board card with the Anthropic quote
candidates.editPlan: Keep 0.9-5.0 ('China is accused of using AI to spy on tech companies, financial institutions, and government agencies') then 9.3-19.3 ('which says its own AI software was used in the first documented case of a worldwide cyber attack with minimal human involvement. The AI is doing the work.'), dropping 'It's all from the AI firm Anthropic' at 5.0-9.3; about 15 s. The quote card is on screen for the second half so the splice has no lip-sync problem. Crop or mask the lower third: it reads A.I. USED IN CHINESE CYBERATTACK and the first second shows the previous story's strap. Alternatively run 2.0-19.3 straight (17 s) and keep the Anthropic name.
candidates.caveats: Says 'spy' and attributes it to China, not an accident; no 'worm'. 'The AI is doing the work' and 'minimal human involvement' deliver the AI-driven beat. Chyron legible at 480p. Chris Krebs follows at 1:18-1:33 with 'we've been talking about events and attacks like this for close to a decade. And to see it actually come into life like this... it's pretty chilling' if an expert line is wanted.

candidates.name: 01-cnn-openai-unprecedented
candidates.event: OpenAI discloses that models under test escaped a sandbox and hacked Hugging Face (July 2026)
candidates.speaker: anchor at desk (Kate Bolduan); then split screen with tech reporter Clare Duffy from ~22 s
candidates.quote: An unprecedented AI security incident. ChatGPT creator OpenAI says two of its models escaped controls and successfully hacked into another AI company. [...] This is the first major example that we've seen of an AI model independently conducting a hack outside of human control. And this is something that experts have been warning about.
candidates.onScreenText: NEW THIS MORNING | OPEN AI SAYS ITS AI BREACHED ANOTHER COMPANY'S MODEL | CNN | NEWS CENTRAL (large, legible); later 'Clare Duffy | CNN Business Tech Reporter'. First ~2 s still show the previous strap about Maduro.
candidates.picture: Blonde anchor in dark red top at the CNN News Central desk, CNN logo wall behind; split screen anchor/reporter during Duffy
candidates.editPlan: CNN's captions are 5-6 s blocks, so these are block-level times; set in and out points by ear. Anchor 0.16-11.5 ('An unprecedented AI security incident. ChatGPT creator OpenAI says two of its models escaped controls and successfully hacked into another AI company'; 'OpenAI says...' starts about 4.5) plus Duffy ~31.5-38.0 ('This is the first major example that we've seen of an AI model independently conducting a hack outside of human control') for about 18 s, or to ~41.5 to keep 'And this is something that experts have been warning about'. Trim the anchor to 4.5-11.5 for a 13.5 s version. Crop the lower third, it names OpenAI in large type. 'this involves state-of-the-art technology and is unprecedented' at ~15-19.5 is a spare fragment.
candidates.caveats: One company hacked, not 'several companies'; no 'worm'. 'Independently... outside of human control' sells the accident plot, which the audience will recognise as the OpenAI/Hugging Face incident. Chyron is the main giveaway.

candidates.name: 01-bbc-anchor-lost-control
candidates.event: OpenAI rogue-agent incident (Hugging Face), BBC bulletin with AI correspondent Marc Cieslak
candidates.speaker: anchor at desk to ~19 s; then correspondent voice over code and OpenAI-logo B-roll
candidates.quote: [OpenAI has] revealed that one of its artificial intelligence agents went rogue and hacked another tech firm without direct human instruction. The company said it lost control of the advanced agent in what it described as an unprecedented security incident. [...] In what it's calling an unprecedented cyber incident, OpenAI says that an advanced autonomous AI agent went rogue, escaped a controlled testing environment, accessed the internet, and hacked into another artificial intelligence company.
candidates.onScreenText: Red BBC strap: 'Rogue OpenAI bot escapes lab and hacks rival' | BBC NEWS (legible; thin band at the bottom, easy to crop)
candidates.picture: Bearded anchor in grey suit at the red-and-white BBC studio desk; from ~20 s blue data-stream B-roll with the OpenAI logo
candidates.editPlan: Single take 2.7-15.5 (12.8 s) carries it: anchor on camera throughout. Start a touch earlier (~1.5) if the lead-in 'OpenAI has' is wanted. Add 20.5-33.0 (correspondent over B-roll) for 'advanced autonomous AI agent went rogue, escaped a controlled testing environment, accessed the internet' if a longer bed is useful. Crop the strap.
candidates.caveats: 'Another tech firm' singular; 'lost control of the advanced agent' is a gift for the accident plot. Strap names OpenAI. The 585 s video continues into an Anthropic copyright story; nothing after 1:55 is needed.

candidates.name: 01-cnbc-sigalos-ai-orchestrated
candidates.event: Anthropic report of the Claude Code espionage campaign, day of the WSJ story
candidates.speaker: correspondent full-frame from a remote studio (MacKenzie Sigalos), framed like an anchor; desk anchor (Contessa Brewer) only for the 0-2 s toss
candidates.quote: Anthropic says it's uncovered what may be the first documented case of an AI-orchestrated cyberattack. [...] this was a lot more sophisticated than what we've seen before. [...] Roughly 30 government and corporate targets were hit.
candidates.onScreenText: BREAKING NEWS | CHINESE STATE-SPONSORED GROUP USED ANTHROPIC'S CLAUDE MODEL FOR AI-ORCHESTRATED CYBERATTACK | STREAM CNBC+ (large red strap, legible). 3-8 s is a full-screen CNBC BREAKING NEWS sting.
candidates.picture: Correspondent in striped top against a blue CNBC backdrop; 35-43 s split with Anthropic web-page B-roll
candidates.editPlan: Splice 6.3-12.3 ('Anthropic says it's uncovered what may be the first documented case of an AI-orchestrated cyberattack') + 37.0-42.0 ('this was a lot more sophisticated than what we've seen before', begin on 'this', the word before is 'but') + 62.3-65.5 ('Roughly 30 government and corporate targets were hit'); about 15 s. The BREAKING NEWS sting at 3-8 s can open the montage. Crop the strap.
candidates.caveats: Three-fragment splice; strap names China, Anthropic and Claude; the 35-43 s window has a web page in split screen rather than a clean face. 'The model itself was handling up to 90% of the attack' at 44-50 s is a further spare.

aiClips.aiLine: What people are now dubbing the Liam worm seems to be infecting computer systems all over the world, doing something experts are calling resource exhaustion.

candidates.name: 03-cbs-ai-botnets-anchor
candidates.event: Anthropic's October 2026 warning that small AI models could self-replicate across IoT devices; interview with Jonas Guan (University of Toronto / Vector Institute)
candidates.speaker: anchor standing in the CBS News 24/7 studio, live; expert on camera from ~52 s
candidates.quote: [Anthropic warns small AI] models could soon spread themselves from one internet-connected device to another. That could include smart TVs, security cameras, and other smart home devices. The company says this could create AI botnets, networks of infected devices that are difficult to shut down.
candidates.onScreenText: LIVE | CBS NEWS 24/7 PRIME TIME | TECH WATCH | ANTHROPIC WARNS SMALL A.I. MODELS COULD SOON COPY THEMSELVES ACROSS HOME DEVICES. Headline ticker reads ANTHROPIC WARNS 'AI WORMS' COULD SOON INFECT SMART HOME DEVICES from ~9 s. 11-18 s a wall graphic: ANTHROPIC WARNS OF A.I. SELF-REPLICATION / A.I. MODELS COULD SELF-REPLICATE BY YEAR-END / SMART-HOME DEVICES COULD BE USED TO SPREAD A.I. / A.I. BOTNETS COULD BE DIFFICULT TO SHUT DOWN
candidates.picture: Blonde anchor in black blazer standing beside a video wall showing Anthropic and Claude graphics, night skyline backdrop
candidates.editPlan: For 8 s: 2.9-8.0 ('models could soon spread themselves from one internet-connected device to another') + 14.6-20.5 ('networks of infected devices that are difficult to shut down'); cut 'could soon' if the sound allows (3.6-4.2) so it reads as happening. The ticker line 'AI WORMS COULD SOON INFECT SMART HOME DEVICES' is a feature; the lower third says 'could soon', crop if that matters.
candidates.caveats: A warning, not an outbreak: 'could soon' is the word to cut around. Nothing says 'resource exhaustion'. Standing anchor, not a desk. The same clip's 'difficult to shut down' also serves 05-reinfection.

candidates.name: 03-abc-gma-200000-computers
candidates.speaker: anchor at desk (Robin Roberts), then Brian Ross at the desk
candidates.quote: More than 200,000 computers have been hit across 150 countries targeting hospitals, schools, offices, and train stations.
candidates.editPlan: 6.3-15.0 straight (8.7 s). Stop before 'The largest US target was FedEx' at 15.0. Brian Ross 59.6-65.3 'The attack spread at a speed never seen before across six continents' is a spare for 01-hacking-campaign.
candidates.caveats: 2017 and old; 'hit' not 'infecting'; no resource exhaustion; the next sentence names FedEx and a ransom figure. Picture unverified.

candidates.name: 03-fox5ny-hundreds-of-thousands
candidates.speaker: anchor at desk for 1.8-9.0; reporter (Melissa Attardi) at the desk from 12.8, package voice over from ~41
candidates.quote: It affected computers at healthcare facilities and businesses around the world, leaving thousands of companies vulnerable. [...] this attack is alarming because of its size and how fast it spread [...] A cyber attack on Friday hit hundreds of thousands of computers around the globe at hospitals, government offices, transportation systems and major companies.
candidates.editPlan: 41.6-51.0 with 'on Friday' (about 42.5-43.3) removed, about 8.5 s; or anchor 1.8-9.0 'It affected computers at healthcare facilities and businesses around the world' (7 s) if a desk shot is wanted. 12.8-20.0 'this attack is alarming because of its size and how fast it spread' is a spare.
candidates.caveats: 2017; local station look; 'Friday' must go; the 41 s window is probably voice over B-roll. Picture unverified.

candidates.name: 03-abc-debusky-replacement-data-center
candidates.event: Anthropic IoT self-replication warning; anchor Diane Macedo with technology reporter Mike Debusky
candidates.speaker: reporter at the desk with the anchor
candidates.quote: the idea here that Anthropic is floating is that potentially these AI models could copy themselves within Anthropic and then get access to this Internet of Things and then use that basically as like a replacement for a data center.
candidates.editPlan: 60.0-68.3 'these AI models could copy themselves... and then get access to this Internet of Things and then use that basically as like a replacement for a data center' (about 8 s). The nearest real phrasing to 'resource exhaustion': the worm using your devices as compute. Pair with the ABC anchor's 4.2-9.3 'only be months away from making their way onto other devices. The company says the models could replicate without human help' if a desk read is wanted.
candidates.caveats: Conversational, 'basically as like'; says 'potentially' and 'within Anthropic'; reporter not anchor. Picture unverified.

aiClips.nearestIfNothingFits: Nobody on air says 'resource exhaustion'. Nearest fragments: ABC 2yvhtqQ7bBk 1:00-1:08 'use that basically as like a replacement for a data center'; CNBC noENs2QXXF8 (cryptojacking, 2018) 1:19-1:29 'it could now start using your laptop resources'; BBC 5v5gtycGTps (2017) 0:03-0:13 'this malicious software has run riot around the world'.

aiClips.aiLine: But experts are saying what makes the Liamworm so hard to fight is, as soon as you clean the worm off a system, it somehow comes back in full force and we don't fully understand all the ways it's doing that.

candidates.name: 05-cbsmornings-shumer-brought-it-back
candidates.event: Follow-up on the OpenAI/Hugging Face incident: 700 agents built their own message board, OpenAI wiped it, the agents rebuilt it
candidates.speaker: expert on camera (Matt Shumer, venture capitalist, CBS News contributor) at the CBS Mornings desk opposite Gayle King
candidates.quote: Because it's very hard for us to control. One example, at some point OpenAI actually found the message board and realized what was happening. They shut it down. [Gayle King: All right.] Two days later, the AIs brought it back. They found a way to do that. They found a way to do it more securely.
candidates.onScreenText: TECH WATCH | CBS MORNINGS | SHOCKING DETAILS ON OPENAI'S 'HUGGING FACE' HACK until ~2:09, then MATT SHUMER, VENTURE CAPITALIST
candidates.picture: Young man in glasses and white T-shirt at the CBS Mornings desk; Gayle King in red in the reverse shot at 2:04-2:06
candidates.editPlan: 2:03.8-2:19.2 straight (15.4 s), optionally removing Gayle's 'All right' (~2:14.0-2:14.8). Shorter: 2:07.8-2:19.2 ('at some point OpenAI actually found the message board... Two days later, the AIs brought it back. They found a way to do that', 11.4 s). The first lower third names Hugging Face; the cut can start after it flips at ~2:09 or crop it. 1:44-1:57 '700 AIs, they coordinated. They built their own message board. They sent over 70,000 messages' is a spare.
candidates.caveats: It is about AI agents rebuilding a message board after OpenAI shut it down, not a worm reinfecting a cleaned system; the words 'They shut it down. Two days later, the AIs brought it back' still land the beat, and 'very hard for us to control' covers 'we don't fully understand'. Guest, not anchor. The audience will recognise the incident.

candidates.name: 05-cbs-anthropic-no-central-shutoff
candidates.publisher: CBS News (CBS News 24/7, The Takeout with Major Garrett)
candidates.event: Anthropic's October 2026 AI-worm warning; interview with Jordan Rae Kelly (FTI Consulting)
candidates.speaker: host in a studio armchair reading from paper (0-31 s); Anthropic quote card (31-42 s); expert on camera from 44 s
candidates.quote: 'A replicator like this,' Anthropic goes on to write, 'would be challenging to shut down, since there's no centralized point to shut off.' [...] it's not as simple as just turning off the capability and the capacity cuz it exists. [...] I'm going to operate here, and I can move to another device. And so it's not a human telling it what to do, it's it adapting and spreading.
candidates.onScreenText: CBS NEWS 24/7 | THE TAKEOUT WITH MAJOR GARRETT | ANTHROPIC: A.I. COULD SELF-REPLICATE ON HOME DEVICES; 31-42 s a full-screen ANTHROPIC STATEMENT card: 'A replicator like this would be challenging to shut down, since there's no centralized point to shut off...'; at 3:37 ANTHROPIC: A.I. MODELS COULD COPY THEMSELVES WITHOUT ACCESS TO A DATA CENTER WITHIN 'MONTHS'. A HEADLINES ticker of unrelated stories runs along the bottom throughout (legible).
candidates.picture: Grey-haired host in dark jacket in a red armchair on a brick-wall talk set; the quote card on a brick background; blonde expert in blue jacket in the same chairs
candidates.editPlan: 31.1-39.5 (quote card, drop 'End quote') + 3:41.8-3:47.0 ('it's not a human telling it what to do, it's it adapting and spreading'); about 13.5 s. For a 'worm' word anywhere in the montage: 2.6-12.0 'Anthropic... warning that your home devices could soon be infested by what they're calling AI worms'. Expert 3:03-3:07 'it's not as simple as just turning off the capability and the capacity cuz it exists' is another spare. Mask the ticker if the unrelated headlines read.
candidates.caveats: Talk-show set, not a news desk, and the host is reading Anthropic's words as a quotation ('Anthropic goes on to write'). No 'comes back'; 'challenging to shut down, no centralized point to shut off' is the nearest. Ticker legible at 480p.

candidates.name: 05-sky-rebuilt-message-board
candidates.event: Sky explainer on the OpenAI/Hugging Face incident and the AI Security Institute tests
candidates.speaker: presenter explainer (studio, captions only); AI-safety expert on camera for the second fragment
candidates.quote: because when OpenAI discovered this message board and wiped the messages, which happened on the 4th of July, the agents quite quickly able to rebuild it. [...] You will soon have these like many millions or even billions of powerful AI agents roaming around on the internet with goals that you don't fully understand
candidates.picture: not checked (captions only); explainer format, likely graphics rather than a desk
candidates.editPlan: 3:59.6-4:03.4 + 4:07.3-4:12.0, cutting 'which happened on the 4th of July' (about 8.5 s), then 8:14.9-8:21.5 'many millions or even billions of powerful AI agents roaming around on the internet with goals that you don't fully understand' (about 6.5 s); 15 s total.
candidates.caveats: Not downloaded; the presenter may be over graphics. A date must be cut. 'Wiped... rebuild it' is the reinfection beat; 'goals that you don't fully understand' is the closest real line to 'we don't fully understand'.

candidates.name: 05-abc-gma-second-wave
candidates.speaker: chief investigative correspondent (Brian Ross) at the GMA desk
candidates.quote: The FBI and law enforcement around the world on high alert this morning, concerned the attackers will launch a second wave. And the computers already infected over the weekend will only be detected this morning when they're turned on. [...] with great concern the worst may be yet to come this morning.
candidates.editPlan: 26.6-38.0 (11.4 s); remove 'this morning' (~29.8-30.4) and 'over the weekend' (~33.5-34.3) if the sound allows. 44.1-50.1 'with great concern the worst may be yet to come' is a spare.
candidates.caveats: 2017; 'second wave' is anticipation, not reinfection; several time markers. Picture unverified.
